body.statement: For the full tuple space \(\Theta_n\), without the balanced one-block restriction and without common anchors, graph-gap, or bounded-incidence restrictions beyond quantitative overlap Grams, is there a randomized polynomial-time procedure \((\widehat L_n,R_n)\in\mathcal H_{\alpha,n}\) and a constant \(c>0\) such that \[\sup_{\vartheta_n\in\Theta_n}\mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_{\vartheta,n},\Xi_n,\Zeta_n}[R_n]\lesssim\mathfrak R_n\quad\text{and}\quad\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\ge c\mathfrak R_n?\] The handle is an overlap-aligned tangent packing in the tuple-indexed experiment, paired with nonorthogonal transport or synchronization on the unanchored chart graph.
body.justification: This is the load-bearing open content needed for a matched all-wedge minimax characterization rather than a common-anchor upper theorem.
body.gap: Carpentier and Nickl use isotropic trace-regression mixtures, while Yan and Wainwright use scalar local bounds; neither treats exact-rank tuple-indexed alternatives over every deterministic staircase.
body.consumer: A positive answer would determine when global counterfactual uncertainty is intrinsic to the wedge rather than to a particular synchronization scheme.

obligation.what_is_open: A single all-procedure lower comparison and randomized polynomial-time upper certificate, both uniform over every admissible deterministic staircase wedge and both matching the wedge tangent modulus up to constants.
obligation.obstruction: Quantitative overlap of each observed chart does not itself provide a common anchor, a spectral gap for the chart connection graph, or bounded chart incidence. The available block identity is chartwise, but it does not control the conditioning accumulated when incompatible local gauges are transported around an arbitrary overlap graph. On the converse side, a tangent perturbation that nearly attains the nuclear modulus need not admit a fixed-rank retraction that preserves every overlap Gram, strong-factor bound, and incoherence bound while retaining both its missing-wedge separation and a small observed Gaussian divergence.
obligation.attempted: The constructive route was chartwise spectral truncation followed by orthogonal synchronization and one-step Gaussian correction; without graph-gap and incidence bounds, its propagated operator norm cannot be bounded by the stated modulus. The converse route was the prescribed overlap-aligned Varshamov--Gilbert packing followed by a fixed-rank exponential-map retraction; the chartwise least-Gram directions can conflict on overlaps, so no uniform packing cardinality and separation bound was obtained. The balanced one-chart construction avoids both failures and is proved separately.
obligation.partial_result: The balanced rank-one one-block interior is closed by Theorem \ref{thm:balanced-frontier}: for every fixed \(\mu>1\), its minimax expected honest radius is \(\Theta(\sigma\sqrt n)\), with both a total polynomial-time upper certificate and an all-procedure lower bound. Lemma \ref{lem:block-transport} also gives an exact computable completion map on every individually full-rank four-block chart. What remains unproved is a uniform comparison with \(\mathfrak R_n\) for every admissible deterministic staircase without common anchors, graph-gap, or bounded-incidence hypotheses.
